To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+0+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
